items.note: Remains resolved on the new bytes. The only learner-text change since the fbdd319d recheck is the added opening pair in the 'Now install on your own computer' paragraph: 'These lesson pages run in your browser and need nothing installed. The coding labs run as real Java projects on your own computer, so they need JDK 25 and Maven, and you edit them in the IDE.' It is accurate: the page's activities are explicitly simulated (practice terminal, practice IDE settings), and the java-basics coding lab README and lab.json confirm a local Maven project (starter/pom.xml, prerequisites JDK 25 and Maven 3.9 or later, mvn -q -o test, opened in IntelliJ IDEA or VS Code). It invents no support or IDE arrangement, matches the page's own 'This course uses IntelliJ IDEA' line, and gives the recap a clear why before the numbered steps. The four numbered steps, network-access statement, expected java -version / javac -version / mvn -v output with 'all three show 25', troubleshooting with the stop-and-ask-your-instructor boundary, the ARM-based Windows boundary, and the IntelliJ IDEA starter/pom.xml and SDK 25 check are byte-for-byte unchanged.
